resources.string: On the laptop, run %1$s. It shows the address, a one-time code and the certificate fingerprint.
Wi-Fi or Tailscale address. Port 8760 if you leave it out.
Shown in the laptop\'s device list
This phone was removed from the laptop. Pair it again.
The pairing stored on this phone can\'t be used any more. Pair it again.
The laptop at %1$s answered with this certificate. All 16 groups must match what pair shows on the laptop.
A code works once and expires after 5 minutes. Run %1$s again on the laptop for a new one.
Enter the IP address, like 192.168.1.23 or 100.101.102.103
The port must be a number from 1 to 65535
Only a home or office Wi-Fi address (192.168.x, 10.x, 172.16–31.x) or a Tailscale address (100.64–127.x) works. Aristotle never connects over the public internet.
Can\'t reach this address. Check it, and check that aristotle-server is running on the laptop.
The laptop doesn\'t accept this phone on that address (different network). Use another address that pair shows.
Something answered here, but without a certificate. Use an address that pair shows.
Not paired. Another device may be answering at this address. Check that the phone is on your own Wi-Fi or Tailscale and that the address is the one pair shows.
The certificate changed after you compared it. Not paired; start again.
The laptop could not save this phone. Run %1$s again.
The laptop paired this phone, but the phone could not lock the pairing in its key store. Run %1$s again on the laptop, then pair again.
Sessions open in Hermes on the laptop show up here.
aristotle-server on %1$s answered, but Hermes is not running there. Start Hermes on the laptop; Aristotle reconnects by itself.
Hermes on %1$s now speaks a newer protocol than this aristotle-server knows, so the server stopped relaying to stay safe. Update aristotle-server on the laptop.
Hermes on %1$s answered, but the session list failed. Retry; if it keeps failing, check Hermes on the laptop.

Aristotle refused to connect: %1$s answered with a different certificate than the one you confirmed when pairing. If aristotle-server\'s key was deleted, pair again. Otherwise another device may be answering at this address.
The laptop at %1$s doesn\'t answer on Wi-Fi or Tailscale. Check that it\'s awake and that aristotle-server is running.
Tailscale may be off on this phone. Away from your Wi-Fi, Aristotle reaches the laptop only through Tailscale.
The laptop at %1$s answered, then the connection ended.
Aristotle hit an unexpected error while connecting to %1$s. It tries again by itself.
Android\'s key store did not open this phone\'s pairing with the laptop. This is usually brief, right after the phone starts. Retry; if it keeps failing, pair again.
Keeps the link to Hermes open while Aristotle is closed. Silent.
A Hermes session finished its turn.
Hermes asks for an approval or an answer.
Wants to run a command. Open Aristotle to answer.
Wants your approval. Open Aristotle to answer.
Has a question. Open Aristotle to answer.
Aristotle tells you when a turn finishes or Hermes needs you, also while the app is closed. Android asks next.
While Aristotle is closed, a silent notification keeps the link to your PC so you hear when a turn finishes or Hermes needs you. Stop it from that notification.
Aristotle can\'t tell you when a turn finishes or Hermes needs you.
Settings that keep Android from stopping Aristotle in the background.
HyperOS stops apps in the background. Without these three settings you can miss approvals and “turn finished” alerts.
Android may stop apps in the background to save battery. Without this setting you can miss approvals and “turn finished” alerts.
A HyperOS setting. Aristotle can\'t read it, so tick it when done.
